labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p8_D_cube

hypotheses.paper: W ∈ K(S(n)) (a convex part, the domain of 𝒟 in Prop. 6)
hypotheses.note: IsConvexPart W only; no closedness needed, D(D(D(W))) = D(W) always

genuine facettes: whenever 𝒟(F) is a facette, 𝒟∘𝒟(F) and 𝒟∘𝒟∘𝒟(F) are facettes and 𝒟∘𝒟∘𝒟(F) = 𝒟(F) (prop8_facetteDuale); with 𝒟(∅) defined by Prop. 7's minimality (the α-least facette of D(W)), the identity holds for every extended facette (prop8_facetteDualeExt)

findings: Prop. 8 (l.1072-1074) holds for every convex part W, closed or not, although its proof (l.1076-1077) treats 𝒟∘𝒟(F) as a facette of W (true only for W closed): the 'a fortiori' step goes through with F ⊆ closure(𝒟∘𝒟(F)) in place of 𝒟∘𝒟(F) α F.
questions: OQ-165 (c), live: whether 𝒟 is defined at facettes with D(W_a) = ∅ (where 𝒟(F) = ∅) and at the facette ∅. Reading taken: both, and the row is marked because it holds under both: as an identity of partial maps on genuine facettes, and with 𝒟(∅) := the α-least facette of D(W) (Prop. 7's minimality applied at F = ∅, where every F' qualifies).

labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p9_facette_exposee

hypotheses.note: (facetteDuale W F).Nonempty ∧ facetteDuale (D W) (facetteDuale W F) = F, i.e. 𝒟(F) a genuine facette; under the extended reading (𝒟(∅) the least facette) the statement fails at the interior facette of a full-dimensional W (prop9_ext_imprecise)
any hyperplane (IsHyperplane, Ch. 1 p. 234), not only a supporting one; supports_of_closure_eq shows such a hyperplane supports W

findings: Prop. 9 (l.1087-1090) is false for a convex part W that is not closed, while W ∈ K(S(n)) is the standing domain (Prop. 6, l.1047; K(S(E)) = all convex parts, l.642): in S(2), W = closed triangle minus the vertex s(e1), F = the open edge ]s(e1), s(e2)[ is a facette of W, 𝒟(F) = {s(e0)} is a genuine facette, 𝒟∘𝒟(F) = F, but F̄ contains s(e1) ∉ W, so F̄ is the intersection of W with no hyperplane (FacetteExposeeInstance.not_prop9_nonclosed). The proof's 𝒟∘𝒟(F) « facette de W » (l.1076) presupposes D(D(W)) = W, i.e. W closed. For W closed the statement is proved (prop9_facetteDuale).

Prop. 9 is imprecise if 𝒟 is extended to the facette ∅ of dimension −1 (OQ-165 (c)): for the interior facette F of the closed simplex of S(n), 𝒟(F) = ∅, the extended 𝒟∘𝒟(F) = F, yet F̄ = T is no hyperplane section (prop9_ext_imprecise). The printed proof's « soit p ∈ 𝒟(F) » (l.1093) silently assumes 𝒟(F) ≠ ∅.

The statement's « un hyperplan » is any hyperplane, while the proof's converse (l.1096) starts from « l'hyperplan frontière de D({p}) », a supporting one; the gap is closed in Lean (supports_of_closure_eq: a hyperplane meeting W in the closure of a facette supports W).
questions: Is W closed in Prop. 9 (W a convex body / closed convex, as the proof's « facette de W » for 𝒟∘𝒟(F) and the p. 276 example's « corps convexe » suggest)? Reading taken: closed; without it the statement is refuted (not_prop9_nonclosed).

OQ-165 (c): is « 𝒟∘𝒟(F) = F » meant with 𝒟(F) a genuine facette? Reading taken: yes; under the extended reading the statement is imprecise at the dimension −1 case (prop9_ext_imprecise). The row is unmarked for both reasons.
OQ-160 (a): the proof's « p ∈ W » (l.1097) read p ∈ D(W); the statement is unaffected.

instances: Benzecri.FacetteExposeeInstance.vertex0_section and vertex0_exposee: the vertex {s(e0)} of the closed simplex T of S(n+1) (the closed triangle of S(2) for n = 1) is T ∩ ⟨·,(0,1,…,1)⟩^⊥ and 𝒟∘𝒟({s(e0)}) = {s(e0)} with 𝒟({s(e0)}) genuine (through prop9_facetteDuale's converse)
Benzecri.FacetteExposeeInstance.facetteDuale_interieur, facetteDualeExt_interieur, interieur_not_section: the interior facette of T has 𝒟 = ∅, extended 𝒟∘𝒟 = id, no hyperplane section
kb_proposals: On S(n), D(D(W)) = W̄ is D'_D_eq_closure + D'_dotPairing (D_D_eq_closure here), and D∘D∘D = D holds for every W (D_D_D): state 𝒟-iterates without closedness and rewrite D(D(D W)) = D W inside facette predicates.
